page: Amazon Web Services c8a.24xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features 96 dedicated physical cores and 96 vCPUs running on an AMD EPYC 9R45 processor with a peak frequency of 4.5 GHz. The CPU subsystem provides 48 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache per core, alongside vector instruction support including AVX, AVX-512 (with VNNI and BF16), and SHA extensions. Memory comprises 192.0 GB of DDR5 operating at 6 GHz, establishing a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core.

The server does not include bundled local storage, requiring network-attached EBS volumes for persistent data. The network architecture delivers a baseline bandwidth of 40 Gbps, with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses included. There are no discrete GPUs present in this hardware configuration.

Benchmark results place the c8a.24xlarge in the top tier for raw computational density. It achieved a Geekbench multi-core score of 31,526.0 and a single-core score of 2,819.0, accompanied by a PassMark CPU score of 139,164.12 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 350,848.8. Memory read bandwidth reaches 515.4 GB/sec for uncached blocks and write bandwidth reaches 190.63 GB/sec. Application testing reveals strong throughput across code compilation (97,396.0 on Clang), static web serving (107.42 GB/sec), and Redis SET operations (250.41 million operations per second).

Given its compute-heavy 1:2 memory ratio and high vector instruction throughput, the c8a.24xlarge offers strong qualitative cost efficiency for scale-out compute jobs, software build pipelines, scientific simulations, CPU-based LLM inference, and high-throughput web serving, though data-heavy pipelines must factor in reliance on external storage.
description: Amazon Web Services c8a.24xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by the Nitro hypervisor and AMD EPYC 9R45 processors. The instance provides 96 dedicated physical cores and 96 vCPUs reaching clock speeds of up to 4.5 GHz, supported by 192.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory (2.0 GB per vCPU) and a 40 Gbps network baseline. It includes advanced CPU instruction sets such as AVX-512, VNNI, and BF16, while omitting dedicated GPUs and bundled local storage. In benchmark evaluations, the c8a.24xlarge consistently achieves top-tier scores in multi-core compute tasks, PassMark CPU tests, Redis operations, and software compilation. This instance is best suited for compute-intensive workloads including CI/CD build environments, batch processing, static web serving, scientific simulations, and CPU-driven machine learning inference.
